rationale: Evidence from the largest comprehensive cohort of ACBD6 deficiency (45 affected individuals across 28 families reported by Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2024) directly confirms that dystonia is present in 94% of patients and progressive postural deformities in 97%, whereas parkinsonism/hypokinesia occurs in only 32% of individuals and develops with advancing age. Furthermore, hyperkinetic movement disorder landscape analyses (Morales-Briceño et al.) emphasize axial dystonia rather than parkinsonism as the primary diagnostic hallmark of recessive ACBD6 variants in pediatric neurodevelopmental cohorts. No literature refutes these phenotypic frequencies.

evidence.text: In a multicenter international cohort of 45 individuals with bi-allelic ACBD6 pathogenic variants, dystonia was observed in 94% (42/45), early-onset progressive postural deformities in 97%, while parkinsonism/hypokinesia was detected in only 32% (14/44 assessable) and emerged with advancing age.

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The most conspicuous and common movement disorder was dystonia (94%), frequently leading to early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%), limb dystonia (55%) and cervical dystonia (31%). A jerky tremor in the upper limbs (63%), a mild head tremor (59%), parkinsonism/hypokinesia developing with advancing age (32%) and simple motor and vocal tics were among other frequent movement disorders.

evidence.text: Review and data-driven clustering of hyperkinetic movement disorders in neurodevelopmental syndromes identify axial dystonia as a key phenotypic finding suggesting recessive ACBD6 mutations.

new_directions.question_text: What is the precise median age of onset and progression rate of hypokinesia/parkinsonism in adult ACBD6 patients compared to the onset of axial dystonia?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the longitudinal transition from pure hyperkinetic dystonic-ataxic syndrome to dystonia-parkinsonism will guide age-stratified clinical diagnostics and surveillance.

new_directions.question_text: Does dopaminergic imaging (e.g., DaTscan) show pre-synaptic nigrostriatal deficit in ACBD6 patients who develop hypokinesia versus those who exhibit purely hyperkinetic dystonia?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether parkinsonism in older ACBD6 patients reflects progressive nigrostriatal degeneration or downstream network dysfunction will inform trial design for dopaminergic therapies.
